title: E-bike use in the UK today
text:
##### Sarah Whitebread Head of Policy and Public Affairs

### E-bike use in the UK today

#### Cycling UK

• We are the UK’s cycling charity. 
• Founded in 1878, we speak up for all who cycle to make sure it’s a safe and easy choice for everyone to travel, explore and have fun. 
• We are powered by our heritage and expertise, and the passion of our supporters, campaigners, partners and 70,000 members. 
• Our work spans campaigns, policy, developing new routes, supporting member groups and delivery of behaviour change programmes, either directly or with partners, reaching 130,000 people per year across the UK 

#### Positive impacts of cycling

• Cost of Living 
• Health 
• Environment 
• Economy 
• Road safety 

More detail: IPPR Stride and Ride report, February 2024

#### UK lags behind Europe in e-bike sales

• UK e-bike sales around 146,000 in 2024 (about 9% of bike sales). A 2025 YouGov survey found 85% of British adults say they’ve never used an e-bike. 
• Germany sold over 2 million e-bikes in 2024. Norway and Denmark sold more per capita than any other country (36.2 and 36.1 per 1,000 people). 
• E-bikes account for roughly half of bicycle sales in Germany and the Netherlands. 
• The UK lags leading European markets.

#### Barriers to wider uptake

• High upfront purchase costs 
• Limited affordable finance 
• Concerns about safe infrastructure and secure parking 
• Perceived battery safety concerns and negative media coverage 
• Limited opportunities to try before buying 

#### Subsidy schemes have had big impact across Europe

• In Portugal, the Green Mobility programme covers 50% of the purchase price of an ebike up to a maximum of €750, and 50% of the price of an ecargobike up to a maximum of €1500. The total budget for the scheme is €10 million. 
• A national scheme in France ran from 2017 – 2025, costing the French government €135 million. The scheme included a scrappage scheme and typically 40% discount in purchase costs. 

Map credit: European Cyclists Federation / Wolt Money for Bikes tracker

#### Good local example: Nantes, France

• Targeted incentive: Level of subsidy depends on household income + family size 
• Second-hand bikes are eligible 
• Around 10,000 purchases supported between 2018-2025; annual budget of between €500,000 and €600,000 for the scheme. 
• Complemented by long-term rental scheme; 80% of beneficiaries purchase bike afterwards 

Credit: Holger Haubold, ECF

#### Ebike loans: lessons from Making Cycling E-asier

• National scheme funded by DfT, launched in 2022, delivered by Cycling UK. 
• Originally launched in Sheffield, Leicester, Manchester and Luton 
• Evans Cycles delivering free one-month e-cycle loans 
• Community hubs delivering skills & confidence sessions and one-month loans 
• Workplace hubs delivering skills & confidence sessions and one-month loans to staff 
• Engagement events and opportunities to try 
• With e-cycles from top brands, non-standard cycles and cargo bikes 

#### Programme objectives

1. Get more people to cycle and e-cycle, accelerating the uptake of e-cycles 
2. Accelerate the number of trips by e-cycle replacing motor vehicle journeys 
3. Engage those with a higher propensity to cycle or cycle more often in target geographic areas 
4. Increase awareness and highlight the benefits of e-cycles as a route to increasing cycling 

#### Luton scheme: results

• Participant satisfaction and behaviour change with the programme was high. 
• 97% rated the programme as good or very good (Target of 90%) 
• 70% cycled more often than before their loan 
• Weekly cycle trips to work roughly doubled, from 38% to 75% 
• 63% of e-cycle miles were on journeys of six miles and under 
• The percentage of responders driving on five or more days a week fell from 37% to 28%. 

The largest gains were among responders who were not frequent cyclists at baseline. Their number of cycle trips per week rose to levels comparable with those of established cyclists across every journey purpose measured.

#### Key learnings

1. Opportunities for loans alongside training increases breadth of participants 
2. Cost of purchase / leasing options are key factors in sustained activity 
3. Storage and security are not factors to ignore 
4. Staff led approaches and local hubs encourage the non-regular cyclist 
5. Unexpected benefits of the e-cycle 

#### Impactful stories

Abdul started a new job at Old Trafford. The e-bike loan meant he reduced his commute time by an hour and saved £41 a week on travel which was the same as purchasing an e-bike on finance. A win for lots of reasons, including more time at home with his wife and new baby!

Jane suffered life altering injuries in an accident and could no longer cycle a standard 2-wheel bike. Loaning an e-trike increased Jane’s physical and mental well being and provided independence and a renewed love of cycling she thought was no longer available to her!

It now seem like madness that I was driving around, running an engine and getting stuck in traffic every day. It’s going to take a bit of saving up to buy my own e-cargo bike, but I already know that it will be valuable for myself and my business.

Steve, cargo e-bike loanee, stonemason

#### What we want to see

1. Financial support to buy ebikes from national or local governments (as part of wider ask for approx. 10% transport budget to be spent on active travel) 
2. Expansion of free / low cost leasing schemes across the UK as an introduction to ebikes and chance to “try before you buy” 
3. Action from the Government to keep illegal bikes and batteries off the road 
4. Investment in segregated cycle routes and secure cycle parking to remove additional barriers . . .
